nodes.name: Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam was washed with 3 M HCl and water in the size of 1.5 × 3 cm².

nodes.name: Ni-BDC solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The as-processed nickel foam was immersed into a solution containing 4.5 mL DMF and 1 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O in a Teflon-lined autoclave. Afterwards, a solution composed of 7.5 ml DMF, 1 mmol BDC and 1 ml 0.4 M NaOH was poured into the autoclave and subsequently heated at 100°C for 15 h.

nodes.name: NiRu_x-BDC ion exchange
nodes.procedure: The obtained Ni-BDC was immersed into an ethanol solution containing 50 mg RuCl3 in Teflon-lined autoclave and then heated at 80°C for 12 h. Other samples were prepared in the similar way with an addition of RuCl3 of 20, 75 mg, respectively. And the as-obtained samples were named as NiRu_x-BDC (x represents the molar ratio of Ru:Ni).

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M PBS solution
nodes.source_text: Remarkably, the NiRu0.13-BDC displayed high HER activity with a low overpotential of 36 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² in 1 M PBS solution... only needed an overpotential of 132 mV to reach a high current density of 100 mA cm⁻²... The Tafel slope of NiRu0.13-BDC is 32 mV dec⁻¹... NiRu0.13-BDC had higher Cdl (1.39 F cm⁻²)... TOFs... 0.0091... faradic efficiency... close to 100%... good stability with a negligible current decrease after 30 h test

NiRu0.13-BDC also exhibited the best HER activity among these catalysts with an overpotential of 34 and 13 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH... Tafel slope curves revealed NiRu0.13-BDC possessing smaller Tafel slope (32 mV dec⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM shows lattice fringe spacing of 1.04 nm corresponding to (200) plane of Ni-BDC, unchanged after Ru introduction with no obvious nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM images in Supplementary Fig. 3 revealed the lattice fringe spacing of 1.04 nm, corresponding to the (200) plane of Ni-BDC. After introducing Ru, the lattice fringe spacing kept unchanged and no obvious nanoparticles exhibited.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping show uniform distribution of C, O, Ni, and Ru elements in NiRu0.13-BDC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) of NiRu0.13-BDC in Fig. 1d further demonstrated the elements of C, O, Ni, and Ru distribute uniformly.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks at 462.9 eV and 485.5 eV assigned to Ru^{3+}; Ni 2p binding energies at 855.9 eV and 873.2 eV for Ni^{2+}, shifted higher in NiRu0.13-BDC indicating electron depletion; O 1s peaks at 531.3, 532.0, 532.9 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 6, the XPS spectra of the NiRu0.13-BDC demonstrated the coexistence of Ni, Ru, O, and C elements... the Ru 3p peaks located at 462.9 and 485.5 eV were assigned to Ru^{3+} 3p... The Ni 2p spectra of Ni-BDC show two characteristic peaks at 855.9 and 873.2 eV... The Ni 2p binding energy of NiRu0.13-BDC is higher than that of Ni-BDC... The O 1s spectra... can be deconvoluted into three peaks with their binding energies at 531.3, 532.0 and 532.9 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES threshold at 22129.17 eV between Ru foil (22127.02 eV) and RuO2 (22130.25 eV), average Ru valence +2.67; Ni K-edge shifts positively confirming Ni-Ru electron interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a... show the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) of RuO2, Ru foil and NiRu0.13-BDC... the threshold value (E0) of the NiRu0.13-BDC (22129.17 eV) is between RuO2 (22130.25 eV) and Ru foil (22127.02 eV)... the average valance state of Ru atoms in NiRu0.13-BDC is +2.67... the energy of Ni positively shifted to higher in comparison with Ni-BDC

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows only Ru-O peak at 1.5 Å, no Ru-Ru peaks confirming atomic dispersion of Ru single-atoms in Ni-BDC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) of NiRu0.13-BDC shows only a primary peak at 1.5 Å, which is assigned to Ru–O bond. Compared with Ru foil and RuO2, there are no obvious characteristic peaks can be identified to Ru–Ru metallic bond
